intro: すら points at the case at the very bottom of the scale, the one you would least expect to fail or most expect to be easy, and says that even it is affected, so everything else obviously is too. It is the written, more formal partner of さえ in its even sense, and lives mostly in negative or surprising statements.

skills.rule: To say even X in a formal or written sentence, put すら after X in place of は, が or を, almost always with a negative or surprising predicate.
skills.explain:
すら marks the most extreme case so the rest of the scale follows: 名前すら書けない (he can't even write his name, let alone anything harder). It usually comes with a negative or with surprise: 当時は電話すら珍しかった (back then even telephones were rare). The tone is written, serious or literary; in conversation さえ or も is more usual.

すら replaces は, が and を: 水すら飲めない, never 水をすら. Other particles stay in front of it: 親にすら, 日本ですら. For a subject, ですら is common: 専門家ですら分からない (even experts don't know).

The key limit: すら means only even. It does not form the if-only condition, so お金さえあれば cannot become お金すらあれば. Use さえ for that. Against も: 名前も書けない is the plain everyday way to say the same thing; すら adds emphasis and a formal register. だけ goes the other way (only X), and こそ picks X out as the right one, with no surprise.

examples.jp: 忙[いそが]しくて、休[やす]む時間[じかん]{すら}ない。
examples.en: I'm so busy I don't even have time to rest.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は自分[じぶん]の名前[なまえ]{すら}書[か]けなかった。
examples.en: He couldn't even write his own name.

examples.jp: 当時[とうじ]は電話[でんわ]{すら}珍[めずら]しかった。
examples.en: In those days even telephones were rare.

examples.jp: 親[おや]に{すら}本当[ほんとう]のことを話[はな]せなかった。
examples.en: I couldn't tell the truth even to my parents.

examples.jp: 専門家[せんもんか]で{すら}その原因[げんいん]は分[わ]からない。
examples.en: Even experts don't know the cause.

contrast.note: In the even sense they are interchangeable; さえ is the everyday choice and すら sounds more written. Only さえ forms the if-only condition: お金さえあれば.
名前も書けない also means can't even write his name, but neutrally. すら stresses that this is the most extreme case.
だけ limits: 水だけ飲んだ is I drank only water. 水すら飲めなかった is I couldn't even drink water. Opposite ends of the scale.

mistakes.bad: お金[かね]{すら}あれば、旅行[りょこう]に行[い]けるのに。
mistakes.good: お金[かね]{さえ}あれば、旅行[りょこう]に行[い]けるのに。
mistakes.note: If only X is さえ...ば. すら only means even, never if only.

mistakes.bad: 水[みず]を{すら}飲[の]めなかった。
mistakes.good: 水[みず]{すら}飲[の]めなかった。
mistakes.note: すら replaces を, が and は instead of following them.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]が{すら}知[し]らなかった。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]で{すら}知[し]らなかった。
mistakes.note: Never が plus すら. For an even-subject use すら alone or ですら.

skills.tip: If let alone the rest fits after X and there is no if, すら works; if there is an if only, switch to さえ.
